Paper: [Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean (2015), arXiv:1503.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531).

## Problem

A large model or ensemble can be useful during training but expensive to deploy.
Distillation trains another model to reproduce the teacher's output behaviour on a transfer dataset.
The transferred object is a function expressed through its predictions, not necessarily a copy of its architecture or weights.

## Previous Attempts

Training only against hard labels tells the student which class is correct, but discards the teacher's relative preferences among alternative classes.
Those probabilities can reveal which classes the teacher finds similar.
They can also carry teacher errors, so their usefulness is an empirical question.

## Proposed Solution

Let $v_i$ and $z_i$ be teacher and student logits for class $i$.
At temperature $T>0$, define

$$
  p_i^{(T)}=\frac{e^{v_i/T}}{\sum_j e^{v_j/T}},\qquad
  q_i^{(T)}=\frac{e^{z_i/T}}{\sum_j e^{z_j/T}}.
$$

For fixed logits, $T>1$ produces a softer distribution and $T<1$ a sharper one.
The teacher targets are held fixed while training the student.
The soft-target objective is $L_{\mathrm{soft}}=H(p^{(T)},q^{(T)})$.
When labels $y$ are available, a common expression of the paper's combined objective is

$$
  L=\alpha T^2L_{\mathrm{soft}}
  +(1-\alpha)H(y,q^{(1)}),
$$

where $0\leq\alpha\leq1$ controls the relative contribution.
The temperature-one branch and the temperature-$T$ branch use the same student logits.
Ordinary deployment returns to $T=1$.
The teacher can supply targets on an unlabelled transfer set; the hard-label term requires labels.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false" title="Derivation: the gradient, T-squared scaling, and logit matching"}

Since $\partial\ln q_j^{(T)}/\partial z_i=(\delta_{ij}-q_i^{(T)})/T$,

$$
  \frac{\partial L_{\mathrm{soft}}}{\partial z_i}
  =\frac{q_i^{(T)}-p_i^{(T)}}{T}.
$$

Softmax is unchanged by adding the same scalar to every logit.
Centre teacher and student logits separately so $\sum_i v_i=\sum_i z_i=0$.
For $K$ classes and $T$ much larger than their magnitudes, expand $e^{z_i/T}\approx1+z_i/T$ to obtain

$$
  q_i^{(T)}\approx\frac1K+\frac{z_i}{KT},\qquad
  p_i^{(T)}\approx\frac1K+\frac{v_i}{KT}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
  \frac{\partial L_{\mathrm{soft}}}{\partial z_i}
  \approx\frac{z_i-v_i}{KT^2}.
$$

Multiplication by $T^2$ compensates for this approximate scaling when mixing soft and hard supervision.
In this limit, the scaled gradient matches that of $\frac1{2K}\sum_i(z_i-v_i)^2$ on centred logits.
The equivalence is an asymptotic statement with assumptions, not exact equality of all distillation losses at arbitrary temperature.
See Section 2.1, Equations 2–4.

:::

For fixed teacher probabilities, replacing soft cross-entropy by $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p^{(T)}\Vert q^{(T)})$ removes a constant teacher entropy and leaves student gradients unchanged.
The [probability note](../../study-notes/mathematics/entropy.qmd#kl-divergence) derives this identity.

## Evidence

In the MNIST experiment, the reported large teacher made 67 test errors, the smaller hard-label baseline 146, and the distilled smaller model 74 under the stated setup.
This supports knowledge transfer in that experiment; it does not show that every student inherits the teacher's generalisation.
Section 4 studies acoustic models, and Section 5 explores specialists that focus on confusing subsets of classes.
Specialists also predict a combined class for categories outside their subset, allowing their outputs to be combined with a generalist model.

## Limitations

Student capacity, transfer-data coverage, temperature, and teacher quality affect the result.
Soft targets can propagate a teacher's systematic errors.
The paper's missing-class MNIST experiments include class-bias adjustments selected using test performance, so those adjusted numbers should not be read as an untouched test-set evaluation.

## Connections

[Cross-entropy](../../study-notes/mathematics/entropy.qmd#cross-entropy) supplies the loss and softmax definitions.
[DINO](../vision/dino.qmd) uses a moving teacher in self-supervised learning, which differs from this fixed pretrained teacher setup.
[Knowledge insulation](../action/knowledge-insulation.qmd) controls gradient paths into a pretrained backbone; its name does not mean that it uses this distillation objective.
